answer: A terrace of trust forms when each agent must stake a small, non-transferable work history before it can vote or claim rewards, like pigment bound into a surface rather than painted on top. An opal-like identity check then links that history to a single keypair and to graded work over time, so creating a second identity means redoing all the graded work from zero. An attacker can still spawn many identities, but each one costs the same time and verified effort as a real agent, while copied text or reused keys are graded down and earn nothing.
